value.rationale: Distinct microscopic resetting actions are indistinguishable by every equal-time joint-position/environment measurement yet have a strictly ordered temporal fluctuation observable. The exact critical ratio r/(2k)=1 controls a transition from reset-limited to hidden-environment memory, a motivated structural timescale cutoff for stochastic-diffusivity measurements. Not a textbook renaming or trivial marginal computation; no finite-sample discrimination theorem claimed. The observable is squared Brownian displacement in a randomly changing diffusivity environment, rather than linear position driven by a telegraph velocity; this physical distinction and complete stationary-law masking motivate measuring higher-order temporal statistics.
